problem: Determine whether the naturally occurring full-project TypeScript OOM left by the preceding classifier work has a safe minimal fix, after retrieving relevant past Experience and original evidence.

decision.decision_summary: Do not raise the heap again and do not exclude repository areas merely to obtain a green build. Historical evidence already shows 8GB failure and establishes targeted transitive compilation as the honest bounded verification method.
decision.retrieval_contribution: The recovered original evidence directly prevented two unsafe changes: an unsupported heap-only package.json edit and coverage-reducing tsconfig exclusions.

action.action_summary: Fresh-counted 4,711 TypeScript inputs, inspected the largest files and build configuration, followed prior evidence to the 8GB reproduction, made no build/source change, and backfilled only the missing Experience record.

evidence.evidence_detail: exact-key NOT_FOUND disclosed; related Experience retrieved; prior 8GB OOM evidence followed; memory changed the decision; no unsafe build configuration change; 112 canonical records and all 11 GENIE regressions passed after existing-index currency repair.

cause.root_cause_summary: The full-project program includes thousands of large WIP/generated TypeScript files; prior evidence reproduces OOM even at 8GB. The retrieval miss was caused by the prior task ending with Trace+Outcome but no canonical Experience, not by a retrieval-engine failure.

lesson: A remembered limitation should change development behavior: when original evidence already disproves a heap-only retry, preserve honest targeted verification instead of weakening scope for a green signal; separately backfill a real uncaptured outcome without redesigning memory infrastructure.
